claims.claim: Prompt injection is the highest-impact class of risk for LLM applications, enabling data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and tool misuse.
claims.notes: Ranked as the top risk (LLM01) in OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

claims.claim: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibitions applying from 2 February 2025 and most provisions applying from 2 August 2026.
NIST AI RMF defines four core functions - Govern, Map, Measure, Manage - applied across the AI lifecycle.
claims.notes: Core framework structure of AI RMF 1.0.

claims.claim: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the first certifiable AI management system (AIMS) standard.
Agentic AI introduces new risk categories including tool poisoning, delegation abuse, inadequate oversight, and unbounded autonomy.
claims.notes: OWASP Agentic AI threats and mitigations publication.

claims.claim: Sensitive data leakage via model outputs and training data extraction are material privacy risks for LLM systems.
claims.notes: LLM09 Sensitive Information Disclosure in OWASP Top 10 for LLM.

claims.claim: High-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act will require conformity assessment, risk management, data governance, and transparency obligations before placing on the EU market.
claims.notes: Title III obligations for high-risk systems.

claims.claim: The Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) postponed EU AI Act application for stand-alone high-risk (Annex III) systems to 2 December 2027 and for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028.
claims.notes: In force 27 July 2026; the first substantive amendment to the AI Act.

claims.claim: The Digital Omnibus on AI adds new Article 5 prohibitions for AI-generated child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate imagery, effective 2 December 2026, and sets the watermarking deadline for AI-generated content of tools already on the market to 2 December 2026.
claims.notes: New providers must watermark from first day of market placement after 2 Aug 2026.

claims.claim: In the OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026, Excessive Agency rose to third place (from its prior rank), and System Prompt Leakage was replaced by the broader Hidden Context Exposure category.
claims.notes: The 2026 methodology weighted ~6,639 documented real-world incidents at 25% alongside 75% expert-practitioner consensus.

claims.claim: Agentic and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based tooling is an emerging, actively exploited risk surface, with unauthenticated authentication bypasses and remote code execution reported in AI agent frameworks (e.g., Langflow) since 2026.
claims.notes: CVE-2026-93680 (auth bypass) and CVE-2026-110186 (unauthenticated RCE via MCP tool enumeration) fixed in Langflow 1.13.0.
